questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

80 The individual’s marginal utility of money is $1 = 2 units of utility. What is the maximum quantity of the good that the individual will buy when its price is $6?

options.A: 2 units B 3 units C 4 units D 5 units

questions.questionText: An economist calculates that a firm has incurred the following costs over the course of the year. $(000) wages and salaries 150 opportunity cost of owner’s time 40 materials 80 rent of buildings 30 marketing fees 20 interest on bank loans 25 interest forgone on finance provided by owner 15 depreciation of equipment 20 By how much would the economist’s calculation of the total cost incurred by the firm exceed an accountant’s calculation of the firm’s total cost?

Which feature of an economy would be most favourable for the survival of small firms?

options.C: the presence of a stock exchange
options.D: the widespread availability of bank lending

questions.questionText: The demand for a firm’s product is perfectly inelastic. What will be the effect on the firm’s revenue if it increases its price by 5%?

options.D: Its revenue will fall to zero.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. MC cost, revenue AC MR AR O output The firm changes its objective from sales revenue maximisation to profit maximisation. Which groups are most likely to be winners and losers as a result of this change? winners losers

A firm operates in a perfectly competitive market. Which relationship between the firm’s cost and revenue describes a position where allocative efficiency would be improved if the firm reduces its present level of output?
Which change would make it easier for a cartel to operate effectively?

options.A: an increase in competition from closely related industries
options.B: an increase in the number of firms in the industry
options.C: an increase in the range of products made by cartel members
options.D: an increase in the stability of the market for its products

National income statistics show that real GDP per head is 25% higher in country X than in country Y. Why might this difference exaggerate the gap in average living standards between the two countries?

options.A: Country X has a larger population than country Y.
options.B: Country X has a higher rate of inflation than country Y.
options.C: The proportion of services people provide for themselves is higher in country Y.
options.D: The proportion of the country’s industry which is owned by foreign firms is higher in country Y.

questions.questionText: A country’s central bank engages in a policy of quantitative easing (open market purchase of securities). How is this policy meant to affect the quantity of narrow money and the quantity of broad money? effect on effect on narrow money broad money

According to monetarist theory, what will be the short-run effect on the level of output and on the price level of an unanticipated increase in the money supply? effect on the effect on output price level
Which correctly identifies injections into a country’s circular flow of income? private sector government sector trade sector I > S G > T M > X
Other things remaining unchanged, what is likely to be a consequence of an increase in net cash withdrawals from the commercial banks?

options.B: an increase in the cash reserves of the commercial banks
options.C: an increase in the liquidity of the commercial banks
options.D: a restriction in the ability of the commercial banks to lend

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the determination of the rate of interest in an economy where MS represents the money supply and LP represents liquidity preference. MS LP LP

The table gives the percentage of employment in the primary, secondary and tertiary sectors in four countries. Which country is most likely to be a developing country? primary secondary tertiary sector % sector % sector %
Which policy is specifically designed to reduce the level of structural unemployment?

options.A: an increase in the level of state benefits paid to the unemployed
options.C: a reduction in the level of direct taxation

questions.questionText: What would be most likely to stimulate long-run growth in an economy?

options.B: government policy to raise aggregate demand

questions.questionText: The European Union imposes a quota on the volume of garments imported from Brazil. What is likely to be a consequence?

options.A: a decrease in the price paid by EU consumers for Brazilian garments
options.B: a reduction in the inflation rate in the EU
options.C: a switch to producing lower-value garments by Brazilian textile firms
options.D: the closure of Brazilian-owned textile factories

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, what is likely to result from an increase in interest rates in a country?

options.A: a capital outflow from the country
options.B: a depreciation of the country’s currency

questions.questionText: What is the main objective of supply side policies?

options.A: to bring a country’s potential output up to the level of its actual output
options.C: to ensure that the composition of output matches the pattern of demand
options.D: to increase potential output by increasing efficiency

questions.questionText: What will increase the multiplier effect of an increase in government spending on national income?

options.C: an increase in the marginal propensity to consume
options.D: an increase in the marginal propensity to import

questions.questionText: Without any change in government policy, what will be the effect of an economic recession on tax revenue and on government expenditure? government tax revenue expenditure
